card.description: A binary construction that takes any two rectangular classical parity-check maps and returns one CSS stabilizer code. Its physical qubits are the disjoint bit×bit and check×check pairs of the factors; its X and Z checks occupy the complementary check×bit and bit×check pairs. The shipped repetition-factor instance is only a small visual witness of this general factor-to-output rule, not the definition of the construction or evidence for properties of every HGP output family.

views.description: For H1 of shape m1×n1 and H2 of shape m2×n2, the executable convention is HX = [H1⊗I_n2 | I_m1⊗H2^T] and HZ = [I_n1⊗H2 | H1^T⊗I_m2]. Expanding these two binary blocks gives the ordered sparse-Pauli baseline used by the verifier; no geometric layout or decoder is implied by the matrix formula.

Read each Hi as a map from an ni-dimensional bit space to an mi-dimensional check space. Qubits occupy bit1⊗bit2 and check1⊗check2. X checks occupy check1⊗bit2, while Z checks occupy bit1⊗check2. This four-space typing fixes every transpose and tensor identity before a matrix is multiplied.

The same four spaces form the middle portion of a product chain complex. Applying either factor map in the two possible tensor directions creates the two check blocks. The boundary-of-a-boundary cancellation is exactly the CSS commutator cancellation, so the homological and Kronecker-block descriptions are two readings of one ordered construction.

If ri is the binary rank of Hi, the two qubit sectors contain n1 n2 and m1 m2 coordinates. The logical dimension splits into a kernel–kernel contribution (n1-r1)(n2-r2) and a transpose-kernel contribution (m1-r1)(m2-r2). The general constructor helper recomputes both terms and rejects disagreement with the stabilizer rank.

Factor kernels and transpose kernels supply canonical row- and column-shaped representatives, while quotienting by factor images identifies representatives of the same quantum logical class. These shapes are useful to ReShape and related algorithms; they are not extra logical qubits and do not make an arbitrary correction maximum likelihood.

ReShape uses HGP logical shapes under its stated factor and error conditions; erasure decoders are given the lost support; Viderman-style and iterative decoders require declared expansion or update hypotheses; BP-OSD is a generic sparse-matrix benchmark. These inputs and guarantees are not interchangeable, and none yields one decoder for every binary factor pair and every syndrome model.

A factor symmetry or symplectic matrix first specifies a logical Clifford action. A physical protocol must then realize it by transversal layers, partitions, defects, measurements, or other declared resources, and a fault-tolerance argument must control faults through that protocol. Targeted-Clifford constructions and product-code no-go results constrain different layers, so neither is a construction-wide gate label.

Restricting or coupling the factor matrices creates HGP output subclasses; reducing redundant sectors changes the formula under extra algebraic hypotheses; changing to a multi-factor non-CSS product changes the construction itself; embedding one fixed output in a planar device changes only its realization. Output entries therefore point inward with typed product_of relations rather than being treated as aliases of HGP.

Sparse algebraic checks may still connect distant hardware qubits. A realization must add an interaction graph, ancillas, a measurement schedule, fault propagation, and a decoder for repeated records. Distance-preserving circuits and non-local-resource studies solve declared architecture problems; they are not outputs of the bare tensor formula.

params.L1: Length of the first open-repetition factor in the shipped visual witness; integer L1 >= 2. This is not a restriction on the general HGP operation.
params.L2: Length of the second open-repetition factor in the shipped visual witness; integer L2 >= 2. This is not a restriction on the general HGP operation.

decoders.noise: one finite HGP CSS matrix with perfect X- and Z-syndrome bits; free variables are fixed algebraically without a likelihood model
decoders.notes: This deterministic solver applies to the exported matrix but exploits no HGP logical shape, degeneracy, factor distance, or noise statistics. It is a reproducible baseline, not evidence that arbitrary HGP factors are efficiently decodable.

decoders.noise: sparse finite HGP checks under code-capacity Pauli noise with perfect syndrome and implementation-specific message-passing settings
decoders.notes: BP-OSD is a generic qLDPC benchmark whose post-processing can repair short-cycle failures. Performance on selected HGP matrices does not transfer a threshold, tuning, or asymptotic guarantee to every factor pair.

decoders.noise: arbitrary binary factor pairs with repeated noisy syndrome extraction, routing faults, correlated data faults, and no expansion or erasure side-information assumption
decoders.notes: No uniform construction-wide decoder for this combined regime was found in the primary-source search completed on 2026-08-10. ReShape, erasure, Viderman-style, iterative, and BP-OSD results remain available only under their separate hypotheses.

realizations.platform: routed or non-local HGP syndrome-extraction architecture
realizations.description: Distance-preserving stabilizer-measurement circuits and non-local resource studies provide schedules for declared HGP layouts and interaction models. They do not turn every sparse factor pair into a shallow geometrically local circuit. No generic binary HGP memory with repeated noisy extraction on laboratory hardware was located as of 2026-08-10.

A single-shot preparation proposal uses a higher-dimensional construction and measurement assumptions for declared HGP families. This is a state-preparation protocol under those hypotheses, not a generic constructor feature or a laboratory memory demonstration.

relations.how: Binary HGP is the length-two CSS specialization of the broader homological-product operation on chain complexes. Surface and quantum-expander entries instead point to this construction with typed product_of edges; reversing those edges would confuse an operation with one of its output families.

operations.gate: Hadamard up to logical swaps and control-Z on HGP logical sectors
operations.level: Clifford operations under the paper's logical-basis partition
operations.cost: apply the declared transversal layers and track their simultaneous action on the canonical HGP logical basis; targeted entangling actions require sequences interleaved with error correction, so this is not an arbitrary gate on an unanalysed factor pair

operations.gate: single-block Clifford gates through puncture and wormhole deformation
operations.level: fault-tolerant code-deformation protocol for selected HGP codes
operations.cost: introduce the required defects, modify and measure stabilizers along the deformation path, decode throughout the protocol, and use state injection for the non-Clifford resource; the bare HGP tensor rule supplies none of this hardware or scheduling structure
